translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

The beginning of the Lord’s word that came to Hosea. The Lord said to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a wife who practices prostitution and children who practice prostitution, for the land has given itself completely to prostitution, turning away from following the Lord.”
He went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim as his wife. She conceived and bore him a son.
The Lord said to him, “Name him Jezreel, for in a little while I will hold the house of Jehu accountable for the blood of Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
On that day I will break Israel’s bow in the Valley of Jezreel.”
She conceived again and bore a daughter. The Lord said to me, “Name her Lo-Ruhamah, ‘Not Pitied,’ for I will no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, but will certainly carry them away.
But I will have mercy on the house of Judah and save them by the Lord their God. I will not save them by bow, sword, battle, horses, or horsemen.”
She weaned Lo-Ruhamah, conceived again, and bore a son.
The Lord said to me, “Name him Lo-Ammi, ‘Not My People,’ for you are not my people, and I will not be yours.”

Yet the number of the people of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where they were told, “You are not my people,” there they will be called children of the living God.
The people of Judah and the people of Israel will gather together, appoint one leader for themselves, and come up from the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.
Call your brothers “My People,” and your sisters “Beloved.”
Bring a case against your mother; bring a case against her, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove her prostitution from her face and her adultery from between her breasts,
so that I do not strip her naked and leave her as she was on the day she was born, make her like a wilderness and like a thirsty land, and kill her with thirst.
I will have no mercy on her children, for they are the children of a prostitute.

For their mother practiced prostitution, and the woman who bore them acted shamefully. She said, “I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and water, my clothing and linen, my oil, and everything I need.”
Therefore, look, I will hedge her way with thorns and fence off her paths, and she will not find a way.

She will go after her lovers but will not catch up with them; she will seek them but will not find them. Then she will say, “I will go back to my first husband, because I was better off then than now.”
But she did not know that I gave her grain, wine, and oil, and multiplied silver and gold for her; from it they made Baal.
Therefore I will take back my grain at its appointed time and my wine at its appointed time. I will take back my wool and my linen, which I gave her to cover her nakedness.
Now I will expose her nakedness before her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hand.
I will put an end to all her joy, her festivals, her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her appointed celebrations.
I will devastate her vines and fig trees, of which she said, “These are gifts that my lovers gave me.” I will turn them into a thicket, and wild animals will devour them.
I will punish her for the days of Baal, when she offered incense, put on her earrings and pearls, and went after her lovers, but forgot me, says the Lord.
Therefore, look, I will entice her, lead her into the wilderness, and speak to her heart.

From there I will give her her vineyards and the Valley of Achor, so that her understanding may be opened. There she will humble herself as in the days of her youth, as on the day when she came up from the land of Egypt.
On that day, says the Lord, you will call me “My Husband,” and no longer call me “My Baal.”
I will remove the name of Baal from his mouth, and they will no longer mention his name.

On that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals, the birds of the sky, and the creatures that crawl on the earth. I will abolish the bow, the sword, and warfare from the land, and I will let them dwell securely.
I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you to me in righteousness and justice, in kindness and compassion.
I will betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord.
On that day, says the Lord, I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth.
The earth will answer the grain, the wine, and the oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
I will sow her for myself in the land. I will have compassion on her who received no compassion, and I will call those who were not my people, ‘My people,’ and they will call me, ‘My God.’
The Lord said to me, ‘Go again and love an adulterous woman who loves evil, just as the Lord loves the people of Israel, though they have turned after other gods and loved raisin syrup.’
I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a kor and a half of barley.
I said to her, ‘You must stay with me for many days. You must not prostitute yourself or belong to another man, and I will be with you.’
For the people of Israel will remain for many days without a king, without a ruler, without a sacrifice, without an altar, and without anyone wearing an ephod or offering incense.
Afterward the people of Israel will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king. They will know the Lord and his goodness in the last days.
Hear the word of the Lord, people of Israel, for the Lord has a case against the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, no kindness, and no knowledge of God in the land.
Cursing, lying, murder, theft, and adultery have multiplied, and they have mingled blood with blood.
Because of this, the land will mourn, and all its inhabitants will waste away, along with the wild animals and the birds of the sky. Even the fish in the sea will perish.
For no one judges or rebukes, and your people are like a priest who argues.
You stumbled by day, and the prophet with you also stumbled by night, and your mother fell silent.

My people have fallen silent because they have no knowledge. Because you rejected knowledge, I will reject you from the priesthood. You have forgotten the law of your God; I too will forget your children.
As they increased in number, so they sinned, and they exchanged their honor for disgrace.
They ate the sin offering of my people and set their hearts on their wrongdoing.
The priest will be like the people. I will punish them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
They will eat but will not be satisfied. They practiced prostitution but did not increase in number, because they abandoned the Lord and loved
prostitution. Wine and drunkenness have taken away their understanding.
My people consult their own judgment, and their staff gives them guidance, because a spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have turned away from their God.

They sacrificed on the mountaintops and offered incense on the hills, beneath oak, poplar, and terebinth trees, because their shade is pleasant. Therefore your daughters will prostitute themselves, and your daughters-in-law will commit adultery.

I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because they mingle with prostitutes, and the men offer sacrifices with streetwalkers. A people without understanding goes astray.
You have prostituted yourself, Israel, but do not bring guilt on Judah. Do not go to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear, “As the Lord lives.”
For Israel has rebelled like a cow that rebels against the yoke. Now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in an open space.
Ephraim is a partner of idols; leave him alone.
They have all prostituted themselves and loved shame and fear.
The wind will be bound up in their wings, and they will be ashamed of their altars.
Hear this, priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Listen, royal household! For judgment is against you, because you have become a snare for the watchman and a net spread over Tabor.
The hunters who hunt have hidden a snare, but I will discipline them all.
I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. For now Ephraim has prostituted himself, and Israel has become defiled.
Their deeds do not allow them to return to their God, because a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the Lord.
Israel’s glory will be humbled before him. Israel and Ephraim will stumble in their wrongdoing, and Judah too will stumble with them.
With their sheep and cattle they will go to seek the Lord, but they will not find him, because he has withdrawn from them.
For they have been unfaithful to the Lord, because they have fathered foreign children.
Sound the trumpet in Ramah and the horn in Ramah! Shout in Beth-aven! Behind you, Benjamin!
Ephraim will be ruined on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I have made known what is certain.
The rulers of Judah have become like those who move boundary markers. I will pour out my wrath on them like water.
Ephraim is oppressed and crushed in judgment, because he chose to follow worthless things.
I will be like turmoil to Ephraim and like a lion to the house of Judah.
Ephraim saw his sicknesses, and Judah his pains. Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to King Jareb, but he cannot heal you or cure you of your pains.
For I am like a lion to Ephraim and like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear them apart and go away; I will carry them off, and no one will rescue them.
I will go back to my place until they bear their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they will earnestly seek me.
They will say, “Let us return and go to the Lord, who struck us, and he will heal us; he broke us, and he will bind up our wounds.”
He will revive us in a few days, and on the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.
Let us learn to pursue knowledge of the Lord. His coming is as certain as the dawn. He will come to us like rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.
What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your faithfulness is like a morning cloud, like dew that disappears early.
Therefore I cut down the prophets and killed them with the word of my mouth, and my judgment will go forth like light.
For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and knowledge of God more than whole burnt offerings.
But they, like human beings, violated my covenant, and there they were unfaithful to me.
Gilead is a city of evildoers, stained with blood.
Your strength is like that of a bandit. The priests banded together on the road and committed murder at Shechem, for they did evil.
In the house of Israel I saw a horrible thing: there Ephraim committed prostitution, and Israel was defiled.
For you too, Judah, a harvest is prepared, when I bring back my people's captives.
When I healed Israel, Ephraim's guilt was exposed, along with Samaria's wickedness, because they practiced deceit before me. A thief would come in, and a band of raiders would plunder in the street.
They do not say in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness. Now their schemes will surround them; they are before my face.
With their wickedness they made the king glad, and with their deceit
All their rulers are adulterers, like an oven burning for baking. The one kneading the dough will cease from the city [?] until it rises.
On the day of our kings, the nobles began to rage from wine. They stretched out their hands with the wicked.
For their hearts grew hot like an oven as they lay in ambush. Their anger grew all night, and in the morning it burned like fire and flame.
They all grew hot like an oven and devoured their judges. All their kings have fallen, and none of them calls to me.
Ephraim has mixed with the nations. Ephraim became [?] that was eaten before it was baked.
Thus foreigners consumed his strength, and he did not know it. Gray hair appeared on him, and he did not know it.
Israel's honor was brought low before him, yet they did not return to the LORD their God or seek him.
Ephraim became like a foolish dove with no sense. They came to Egypt and went to Assyria.
Wherever they go, I will spread my net over them. I will bring them down like the birds of the sky, and discipline them according to the report of their testimony.
Woe to them, for they have fled from me! I will bring disaster upon them because they have rebelled against me. For I redeemed them, but they spoke lies against me.
They did not cry out to me with all their hearts, but wailed on their beds. They fight over grain and wine, and they rebelled against me.
I disciplined them and strengthened their arms, but they plotted evil against me.
They turned to nothing and became like a treacherous bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword because of the insolence of their tongues. This will bring them ridicule in the land of Egypt.
Your mouth is like a trumpet, and like an eagle over the house of the LORD, because they have violated my covenant and rebelled against my law.
They called to me and said, "We know you, our God."
Israel has forgotten what is good, and the enemy pursued them.
They appointed kings, but not through me. They assumed power without informing me. With their silver and gold they made idols for themselves, so that they would perish.
They have gone astray through your calf, Samaria, and my anger has burned against them. How long will they be unable to become pure?
For it is from Israel, and a craftsman made it; it is not God. Rather, your calf, Samaria, has become a source of idolatry.
For they sowed the wind and reaped the whirlwind. They have no standing grain, not even an ear that produces flour. Even if they had any, foreigners would eat it.
Israel has been swallowed up. Now they have become like a useless vessel among the nations.
For they went up to Assyria like a solitary wild donkey. Ephraim loved gifts.
Even if they are handed over among the nations, I will gather them, and they will rest a little from the burden of the king and the ruler.
For Ephraim multiplied altars for sin, and they became altars for great sins for him.
I wrote for him the many teachings of my law, but he regarded my words as something foreign.
They offer choice sacrifices and eat the meat, but the LORD takes no pleasure in them. Now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish their sins, and they will return to Egypt.
Israel forgot his Maker and built temples, and Judah multiplied fortified cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will consume their fortifications.
Do not rejoice, Israel, or exult like the nations, for you have strayed from your God and loved gifts from every threshing floor.
They will not be satisfied from the threshing floor or the winepress, and the oil will fail them.
They will not remain in the LORD’s land. Instead, Ephraim will return to Egypt, and they will eat unclean food in Assyria.

They will not pour out wine to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please him. Their bread will be like bread of affliction; everyone who eats it will become unclean. For their bread is for their own sustenance and does not enter the LORD’s house.
What will you do on the day of the festival, on the day of the LORD’s feast?
For they have gone away as plunder. Egypt will gather them, and Memphis will bury them. Foreigners will inherit their precious silver, and thorns will grow in their tents.

The days of punishment have arrived; the days of repayment have drawn near. Israel will know. The prophet is a fool; the man clothed in a spirit of madness is insane. Because your wrongdoing is so great, your insolence has increased.
The watchman of Ephraim is with my God. The prophet is a snare that causes stumbling on all his paths, and there is insolence in the house of God.
They have sunk deep into corruption, as in the days of Ramah. Now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish their sins.
I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness, and I saw their ancestors like an early fig. But they went to Baal-peor and dedicated themselves to shame, and they became unclean like what they loved.
Ephraim’s glory has flown away like a bird, away from childbirth, the womb, and conception.
Even if they raise children, I will bereave them until no one remains. For woe to them! I am exacting retribution from them.
Ephraim—as I saw Tyre planted among its buildings, so Ephraim brought his children out for slaughter.
Give them, LORD, what you will give. Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.
All their wickedness is in Gilgal, for there I hated them. Because of their evil deeds, I will drive them out of my house. I will no longer have compassion on them. All their rulers are rebels.
Ephraim has been struck at the root and has withered, so that it bears no fruit. Even if they bear children, I will put the cherished offspring of their wombs to death.
My God will reject them because they did not listen to him, and they will become wanderers among the nations.
Israel is a spreading vine that bore fruit. As its fruit increased, they multiplied altars; as their land prospered, they built high places.
Their heart is divided, and now they will be found guilty. He will overthrow their altars and plunder their high places.
For now they will say, “We have no king because we did not fear the Lord. What can a king do for us?”
They spoke false excuses and made a covenant, and judgment sprang up like weeds in a field of uncultivated land.

The inhabitants of Samaria will become exiles because of the calf of Beth-aven. Its people and its priests will sit mourning over it. They will rejoice over it and over its glory, which has departed from it.
They will also carry it to Assyria as a gift for King Jareb. Ephraim will receive disgrace, and Israel will be ashamed of its own plans.
Samaria has cast off her king like a wave on the surface of the water.
The shrines of Aven, Israel’s sin, will be destroyed. Thorns and thistles will grow on their altars. They will tell the mountains to cover them and the hills to fall on them.
Since the days of Ramah you have sinned, Israel. There they will stand, and war against the children of injustice will not overtake them in Ramah.
With my rebuke I will discipline them. Nations will gather against them when they are punished for their two offenses.
Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh, and I passed over its neck. I will put a rider on Ephraim; Judah will thresh, and Jacob will plunder.
Sow righteousness for yourselves and reap the fruit of kindness. Light a lamp for yourselves, for it is time to seek the Lord until he comes and shows you his righteousness.
You have plowed sin and reaped injustice, and you have eaten the fruit of falsehood, because you trusted in your own ways and in the greatness of your strength.

Destruction will arise among your people, and all your fortified towns will be plundered, like Shalman’s plunder from Bethel on the day of battle, when they dashed mothers to pieces along with their children.
This is what they did to you, Bethel, because of your extreme wickedness. At dawn the king of Israel was shattered and put to shame.
For when Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called him my son.
The more they called them, the more they went away from me. They sacrificed to Baal and offered incense to carved idols.
Yet I led Ephraim and took them into my arms, but they did not know that I healed them.
I drew them with human cords and chains of love. I was to them like someone who lifts the yoke from their necks. I bent down to them, and they ate.
They will not return to the land of Egypt. The Assyrian will be their king because they refused to return.
The sword will grow weak in their cities and disappear from their hands, and they will feed on their own plans.
My people hesitate to return to me. They will call to God, and we will reflect together, but he will not be exalted.
How can I support you, Ephraim? How can I help you, Israel? How can I make you like Admah or like Zeboiim? My heart has changed, and my compassion has been revealed.
I will not unleash my fierce anger, nor will I turn again to destroy Ephraim, because I am God and not a human being. I am the Holy One among you, and I will not enter the city.
They will follow the Lord, who roars like a lion. For he will roar, and the children will come trembling from among the people.
They will come trembling like a bird from Egypt and like a dove from the land of Assyria. I will return them to their dwelling places, says the Lord.
Ephraim and the house of Israel surrounded me with falsehood, and Judah with deceit, until God’s people, a holy and faithful people, went down.
Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the whirlwind all day long. They have multiplied falsehood and plunder. They have made a covenant with the Assyrians and carried oil to Egypt.
The Lord has a case against Judah. He will call Jacob to account for his ways and repay him according to his schemes.
For in the womb he deceived his brother, and in his strength he became great before God.
He overcame the angel’s strength and pleaded with him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with him.
And the Lord God Almighty remembered him.
But you, return to your God. Keep kindness and justice, and wait for your God continually.
Canaan holds deceitful scales in his hand, and he loves to oppress.
Ephraim said, “I have become rich and have found pain for myself. All my labor is not enough for the sin I have committed.”
I am the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. I will again make you live in tents, as in the days of the festival.
I spoke with the prophets, and I multiplied visions. Through the prophets I represented myself in likenesses.
There is pain in Gilead, and in Gilgal you sacrificed bulls for nothing. Your altars too are like heaps in the fields of uncultivated land.
Jacob fled to the land of Aram. Israel worked for a wife, and for a wife he kept watch.
Through a prophet the Lord brought Israel up from Egypt, and through a prophet he was protected.
Ephraim provoked anger and caused bitterness. His blood will be poured out upon him, and his Lord will repay him for his disgrace.
When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling, and he was great in Israel. But he became guilty through Baal and died.

Now they have continued to sin and have made cast images for themselves from their silver, idols in their own likeness, the work of craftsmen. They used to say of them, “They sacrifice human beings and kiss calves.”
Therefore they will be like a morning cloud, like dew that disappears early, like chaff blown from the threshing floor, and like smoke from a window.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. You shall know no god besides me, and there is no savior except me.
I shepherded you in the wilderness, in a desolate, uninhabited land.
I fed them, and they filled their bellies. Their hearts became proud; therefore they forgot me.
I became like a lion to them, and like a leopard on the road to Assyria.
I will meet them like a bear bereaved of her cubs, and I will tear open the covering of their hearts. A lion will devour them there, and wild animals will tear them apart.
I have destroyed you, Israel. Who will help you?
Where, then, is your king, that he may save you and all your cities? And where are your judges, for whom you asked me, saying, “Give me a king and a ruler”?
I gave you a king in my anger, and I took him away in my fury.
Ephraim’s wrongdoing is bound up, and his sin is stored away.
Pains like those of a woman giving birth will come upon him, because he is an unwise son. Now he will not endure the pains of children being born.
I will redeem them from the power of Sheol, and I will rescue them from death. Where, then, is your victory, death? Where is your sting, Sheol? Comfort is hidden from my eyes.

For he will stand apart among brothers. An east wind will come, the wind of the Lord; it will rise from the wilderness, dry up his springs, and make his fountains run dry. He will plunder the treasury of every precious object.
Samaria will be condemned because she rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their children will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.
Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, because you have stumbled through your wrongdoing.
Take words with you and return to the Lord your God. Ask him to forgive your wrongdoing; receive good things, and he will repay you with the fruit of your lips.
And say, “The Assyrian will not save us, and we will not ride on horses. We will no longer call the work of our hands ‘God,’ because you have mercy on the orphan.”
I will heal their turning back and love their vows, and my anger will turn away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel. He will blossom like a lily and put down roots like those of Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree splendid with its fruit, and his fragrance will be like that of Lebanon.
They will be built up and dwell in his shade. They will live on grain and blossom like a vine, and their renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim will say, “What more have I to do with idols?” I have humbled him, and I will make him glorious like a luxuriant fir tree. From me your fruit is found.
Whoever is wise, let him understand these things; whoever is discerning, let him recognize them. For the ways of the Lord are straight: the righteous walk in them, but wrongdoers stumble in them.
